description: A global fashion brand sells articles of clothing in several markets. We have an estimate of how price changes affect sales for each article, assuming constant price elasticity. Price changes must be in multiples of 1 euro. Initial prices for each article are given, and no more than a certain fraction of the prices can change. The new price for each article must be within an allowed range of the initial price. Each article has a maximum production volume; we cannot sell more than that. Given the sales forecast per article for the next twelve months and past elasticities, the goal is to choose new prices for each article to maximize expected revenue.

NumberOfArticles.definition: Number of articles in the assortment

MaxPriceChange.definition: Maximum fraction of prices that can be changed

MaxPriceDeviation.definition: Maximum allowed deviation of each new price from the initial price as a fraction

MaxProductionVolume.definition: Maximum production volume for each article

objective.description: "Maximize the total expected revenue from all articles by choosing new prices, taking into account price elasticities, sales forecasts, and production limits."

constraints.description: The new price of each article must be non-negative
The new price of each article must differ from its initial price by an integer multiple of 1 euro
For each article, the new price must lie within the allowed deviation range: InitialPrice[i] * (1 - MaxPriceDeviation) ≤ NewPrice[i] ≤ InitialPrice[i] * (1 + MaxPriceDeviation)
The number of articles whose price is changed (i.e., NewPrice[i] ≠ InitialPrice[i]) must not exceed MaxPriceChange × NumberOfArticles
For each article, the sales quantity must satisfy 0 ≤ SalesQuantity[i] ≤ MaxProductionVolume[i]
The sales quantity for each article must be consistent with the demand implied by the price elasticity and the chosen new price
